domain: EU chemicals regulation / REACH Candidate List inclusion prediction (substance-level regulatory-outcome task, EU agency publisher)
prediction_question: For a substance identifiable in a documented EU inventory (e.g. the EC Inventory / REACH-registered substances) at a stated instant, will it be identified as an SVHC and included in the REACH Candidate List (published by ECHA under Article 59(10) REACH) within the next window (e.g. 12 months or until the next scheduled update)?
prediction_time: Candidate design (not constructed): a fixed instant before each Candidate List update (updates are irregular, historically ~2 per year; ECHA's own prioritisation document says 'The Candidate List is generally updated twice a year (normally in June/July and in ...)'), with features restricted to regulatory state observable at that instant: harmonised CLP classification (Annex VI as amended by dated ATPs), Annex XIV / Annex XVII / POPs entries (all dated EU legal acts on EUR-Lex), and static identifiers (EC/CAS numbers from the EC Inventory, published in the OJ).
target_definition: Binary: substance included in the Candidate List in the window vs not. Label source: the Candidate List itself (per-entry inclusion date and reason for listing, published on the ECHA website), which would be excluded from shipped features. Positive events: 219+ substances/groups since 2008 per ECHA annual-report figures quoted in searches (read 2026-11-03); clustered by update tranche.

sources.name: ECHA Candidate List of Substances of Very High Concern for Authorisation (Article 59(10) REACH)
sources.access: BLOCKED for this pipeline 2026-11-03: echa.europa.eu sits behind an Azure WAF JS challenge ('One moment, we're checking you're not a bot') that returns 403 to plain HTTP clients (curl with browser UA) and that the supported browser did NOT pass (challenge page persists after 25 s and reload; tab title 'Azure WAF'). data.europa.eu catalogue record 'candidate-list-of-substances-of-very-high-concern-for-authorisation' is stale (modified 2018-06-26, licence null, 0 distributions). The API host chem.echa.europa.eu serves plain clients anonymously (verified: GET .../api-activity-list/v1/authorisationProcess/documents?name=...12th_axiv_recommendation_november2025_en.pdf returned 200, 458,641-byte PDF), but the SPA (ECHA CHEM, IUCDAS) requires JavaScript and its legal-notice route is client-rendered.
sources.licence: Class D for the natural design (see license_evidence): ECHA's own legal notice permits use of website data 'totally or in part' with attribution but PROHIBITS replication of whole or substantial parts of ECHA databases without prior written permission.

sources.name: ECHA legal notice (ECHA CHEM, chem.echa.europa.eu/legal-notice)
sources.access: SPA route; direct curl returns the JS shell (66,311 B, 'You must enable JavaScript'). Text quoted below was read 2026-11-03 from the search engine's index of the same live page (identical clause text returned for three distinct chem.echa.europa.eu routes: /legal-notice, /100.001.000, /100.228.116/obligations).

license_evidence: ECHA legal notice, IP section 4.1.1 (chem.echa.europa.eu/legal-notice, read 2026-11-03 via the search index of the live page; SPA text not curl-extractable): 'the information, documents and data made available on the Website, with the exclusion of materials subject to intellectual property rights or other rights of third parties and whole or substantial parts of databases, may be downloaded, reproduced, distributed and/or used, totally or in part, for commercial and non-commercial purposes provided that: 1. the User acknowledges that ECHA accepts no responsibility... 2. the User does not alter the integrity... 3. ECHA is acknowledged as the source'.

Same notice, immediately following: 'The above general rule of permissibility of downloading and copying information from the ECHA website does not extend to whole or substantial parts of databases... The replication, in whole or in substantial part, of the ECHA databases is prohibited, unless ECHA's prior written permission is given. All requests shall be submitted to ECHA through the information request forms on ECHA's contact page.'

Same notice: 'ECHA reserves the right to block systematic automated data collection activities (including scraping, data mining, and extraction and re-utilisation) of the whole or a substantial part of the Website and the ECHA databases, where justified and subject to applicable law.'

Reading: the Candidate List is a database in the notice's own sense ('a collection of independent works, data or other materials arranged in a systematic or methodical way and individually accessible by electronic or other means'). The natural task ships Candidate-List membership (inclusion date + reason) as the label for the full eligible substance universe, which replicates the list in whole. Features can be kept to EUR-Lex legal acts (freely reusable), but the label cannot: there is no EUR-Lex instrument carrying Candidate-List events (Art. 59(10) publication is ECHA's own act).

measurements.access_measured: 2026-11-03: echa.europa.eu/legal-notice -> HTTP 403 Azure WAF page (9,377 B) with browser UA; supported browser session remained on the challenge page after 25 s + reload. chem.echa.europa.eu root -> 200 (66,311 B SPA shell). chem.echa.europa.eu/api-activity-list/v1/authorisationProcess/documents?name=...pdf -> 200, 458,641 B. data.europa.eu catalogue: GET /api/hub/search/datasets/candidate-list-of-substances-of-very-high-concern-for-authorisation -> 200 (160,913 B JSON): publisher European Chemicals Agency (corporate-body/ECHA), license null, modified 2018-06-26, 0 distributions. Commands in notes.md.
measurements.population_measured: Not measured (licence rejection precedes probing). Publisher-adjacent figures quoted in the 2026-11-03 searches: 'Since 2008, 219 substances or groups of substances have been identified as SVHCs and included in the Candidate List' (ECHA/annual-report PDF via search); EUR-Lex SWD(2018)58: 138 included by end-2012, 174 by 2017; ECHA Annex XIV recommendation approach document: 'The Candidate List is generally updated twice a year'.
measurements.novelty_sweeps: 2026-11-03, 2 web searches: 'machine learning prediction "substances of very high concern" SVHC candidate list REACH' and 'anticipating REACH "candidate list" inclusion prediction regulatory prioritisation chemicals model'. Found: QSAR hazard-property prediction studies that USE the Candidate List as a data set (K-REACH QSAR paper, PMC7451722), organosilicon structure/risk ML, obesogen screening against SVHCs, and expert/rule-based prioritisation schemes (PikMe, Environ Toxicol Chem 2025; semi-quantitative risk-based prioritisation, RSC Sustain 2024). NO published ML benchmark predicting the listing event itself was found. Novelty was NOT the blocker; licence was.

rejection_reason: DROPPED on licence (class D for the natural design; the alternative 'ask ECHA for prior written permission' channel is a class C 'contact us' pattern, which the standing policy closes for new unresolved leads: no unsolicited permission email, no indefinite wait, no invented grant, no extension of another candidate's operator risk acceptance). ECHA's own legal notice permits reproduction of website data in part with attribution but expressly prohibits 'replication, in whole or in substantial part, of the ECHA databases... unless ECHA's prior written permission is given', and reserves the right to block systematic collection. The SVHC inclusion task's label source is the Candidate List itself and a full-population dataset ships exactly that list; there is no EUR-Lex alternative carrying the events. The Azure WAF blocking of echa.europa.eu for both plain HTTP clients and the supported browser is recorded as inaccessible access, NOT as evidence of absent terms - the terms were read from the publisher's own instrument (chem.echa.europa.eu legal notice) and they are decisive.
review: The task itself was strong (novel regulatory-outcome target, real compliance value - listing triggers supply-chain obligations, dated process with a public registry of intentions, ~35 update tranches since 2008, EUR-Lex-derivable as-of features). It dies on the one contract that cannot be redesigned around: the label is an ECHA database and ECHA forbids whole-list replication without written permission.
next_action: Closed. Reopen ONLY on a licence event, not on access improvements: (a) ECHA publishes an explicit open licence covering the Candidate List (a per-dataset CC BY/CC0 statement or documented bulk-data terms permitting redistribution), or (b) the operator records a candidate-specific permission/decision. Do not re-probe the source on access grounds alone; the WAF is not the blocker.
